questions.question: True or false: Rabbi Elazar ben Arakh was one of the five disciples who surrounded Rabban Yochanan ben Zakkai.
options: True
False
questions.explanation: This small group was a spiritual laboratory in which the foundations of rabbinic Judaism were shaped, and in it Rabbi Elazar was identified as the one who outweighs them all.

questions.question: With what image did Rabban Yochanan ben Zakkai describe Rabbi Elazar ben Arakh?
options: An ever-strengthening spring
A plastered cistern that does not lose a drop
Sin-fearing
A threefold cord
questions.explanation: In Avot de-Rabbi Natan he is also called "a flowing stream." The spring is the archetype of the creator, as opposed to the preserving cistern of Rabbi Eliezer.

questions.question: What is the difference between a cistern and a spring, according to the research?
options: The cistern is deeper than the spring
The water of the cistern comes from outside, and the spring wells up from within itself
The spring dries up in the summer and the cistern does not
The cistern belongs to the many and the spring to the individual
questions.explanation: The cistern preserves knowledge learned from a teacher exactly as it is; the spring innovates, deduces one thing from another and develops new branches on the trunk of the tradition.

questions.question: According to the commentators, why does "a good heart" include the answers of the other disciples?
options: Because the heart is the largest organ in the body
Because a good heart means a good memory
Because the heart is the mover of all the other powers
Because a heavenly voice ruled so
questions.explanation: So explained Rabbi Ovadia of Bartenura and the Maharal: the eye sees and the legs walk, but the power that arouses and directs is in the heart.

questions.question: True or false: According to Rabbi Ovadia of Bartenura, anger, worry and envy strengthen the power of memory.
options: True
False
questions.explanation: They "weaken the power of memory." The tranquility that stems from a good heart is a condition for preserving the Torah and developing it.

questions.question: What did Rabbi Elazar propose when his teacher refused to teach him the Account of the Chariot on the road?
options: To return to the study hall and learn there
To ask Rabbi Nechunya ben HaKaneh
To wait until he grew older
"Permit me to say before you one thing that you taught me"
questions.explanation: He did not ask to receive new knowledge, but to show that he "understands on his own" what had already been sown within him, as the Mishnah requires.

questions.question: True or false: When Rabbi Elazar began to expound, Rabban Yochanan ben Zakkai got down from the donkey, wrapped himself in a prayer shawl and sat under an olive tree.
options: True
False
questions.explanation: Getting down from the donkey symbolizes the transition from the material world to the world of the secret, and the recognition that Rabbi Elazar is not merely a student.

questions.question: What happened when Rabbi Elazar expounded on the Account of the Chariot?
options: Fire came down and surrounded the trees, and the trees sang a song
The earth trembled and the donkey fled
Rain fell out of season
A heavenly voice ruled that the halakha follows him
questions.explanation: Rabban Yochanan testified that even the ministering angels accompany them, and kissed Rabbi Elazar on his head.

questions.question: How did Rabban Yochanan ben Zakkai define him after the homily?
options: "A plastered cistern that does not lose a drop"
"One who expounds well and fulfills well"
"Sin-fearing"
"Father of wisdom and father of the generations"
questions.explanation: That is: his most abstract Torah is expressed in the wholeness of his personality and deeds.

questions.question: Why did Rabbi Elazar go to Emmaus after his teacher's death?
options: Because the Romans expelled him from Yavneh
Because his teacher had lived there in his final years
On his wife's advice and because of the pleasantness of the place, certain that his colleagues would come to him
In order to establish the Sanhedrin there
questions.explanation: Emmaus was known for its "beautiful waters and pleasant dwelling." He saw himself as a focal point whom everyone needs, but his colleagues remained in Yavneh.

questions.question: True or false: In Emmaus, Rabbi Elazar's colleagues and disciples gathered around him, as he expected.
options: True
False
questions.explanation: He remained alone. Without colleagues or a teacher, "his learning was uprooted": his Torah was uprooted from him.

questions.question: What did Rabbi Elazar mistakenly read in place of "HaChodesh HaZeh Lakhem" ("This month shall be for you")?
options: "HaChoshekh HaZeh Lakhem" ("This darkness is for you")
"HaChozeh Hayah Libam" ("The seer was their heart")
"HaChodesh HaZeh Libam" ("This month is their heart")
"HaCheresh Hayah Libam" ("Their heart was deaf")
questions.explanation: The one who had been the symbol of the "good heart" became one whose heart was sealed. His colleagues prayed for him and his Torah returned to him.

questions.question: True or false: According to the Gemara, Rabbi Nehorai is Rabbi Elazar ben Arakh.
options: True
False
questions.explanation: "His name was not Rabbi Nehorai but Rabbi Elazar ben Arakh was his name" (Shabbat 147b, Eruvin 13b).

questions.question: What is the meaning of the epithet "Nehorai," according to the Gemara?
options: That he illuminates the eyes of the sages in halakha
That he lived on the bank of a river
That he used to pray at night
That he studied under Rabbi Nechunya
questions.explanation: The name means light. Perhaps it was given to him precisely after his Torah returned to him, as testimony that the light within him had not gone out.

questions.question: From whom did Rabbi Elazar receive the tradition of the crowns on the letters, according to the introduction to "Sefer Tagin"?
options: Rabbi Akiva
Rabbi Nechunya ben HaKaneh
Rabbi Eliezer ben Hyrcanus
Rabban Gamliel
questions.explanation: From Rabbi Elazar the tradition passed to Rabbi Yehoshua ben Hananiah and from him to Rabbi Akiva.

questions.question: True or false: Rabbi Elazar left behind many mishnayot, more than most of his colleagues.
options: True
False
questions.explanation: Their number is surprisingly small. His legacy endured thanks to the quality of his Torah and the direction he charted, and the scarcity of halakhot attests to the forgetting.

questions.question: According to the research, why did Ribaz rule that the spring "outweighs them all"?
options: Because Rabbi Elazar was the most expert in the traditions
Because Rabbi Elazar was the oldest of the disciples
Because after the destruction a creative force was needed to rebuild spiritual worlds
Because Rabbi Eliezer ben Hyrcanus had already been excommunicated
questions.explanation: In a broken world the tendency is to withdraw and preserve, but the real need is for a force that breathes new life.

questions.question: Which saying of Rabbi Nehorai sounds, according to the research, like a confession about Emmaus?
options: "Make for yourself a teacher and acquire for yourself a friend"
"The study is not the main thing but the deed"
"If I am not for myself, who is for me?"
"Go into exile to a place of Torah, and do not say that it will come after you"
questions.explanation: He warns others not to repeat his mistake: to think that his personal understanding would suffice for him without the company of the sages.

questions.question: On which verse did Rabbi Elazar base the washing of hands, and what is the nature of the homily?
options: "And has not rinsed his hands in water"; an asmachta, a hint in Scripture for an enactment of the Sages
"And they shall wash their hands and their feet"; a commandment from the Torah
"And you shall sanctify yourselves and be holy"; a law given to Moses at Sinai
"And that will by no means clear the guilty"; a custom and not halakha
questions.explanation: Thus (Chullin 106a) he sought to connect the everyday commandments of purity to the root in Scripture.

questions.question: What does Rabbi Elazar's "theory of counsel" teach, according to Midrash Tehillim?
options: One must not give counsel without asking the rabbi
Every counsel that is for the sake of Heaven will in the end be fulfilled
Good counsel stems from logical analysis alone
The counsel of the many is always preferable to the counsel of the individual
questions.explanation: Successful counsel stems from purity of heart and intention, and therefore "everyone needs his counsel."
